title: EMPATHIA: Multi-Faceted Human-AI Collaboration for Refugee Integration

bias_targets.methodology: Calculating Cramér's V across 6,359 refugee assessments to detect systematic scoring preferences based on protected demographic categories or country of origin, ensuring no origin-based preferences are present.

Auditing initial model recommendations to detect disproportionate penalization of older refugees (e.g., identifying a 15% penalty for refugees aged 46+) and qualitatively evaluating the ethical agent's ability to challenge ageist assumptions.

Comparing integration recommendations across educational hierarchies (from individuals with basic adult education to those with doctoral degrees) to ensure assessment outcomes are not exclusively dominated by formal educational credentials or traditional economic optimization models.

Qualitatively evaluating the system's ethical agent through case studies to ensure it aligns with anti-discrimination frameworks, protects against exploitation vulnerability, and overrides traditional biases against women (e.g., females in STEM or agricultural contexts).
